anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves f5 from fails to holds exactly as intended: the exit check names the elapsed deadline (12:15:00Z recorded, 12:15:01Z now), states the only own push was at 12:00 and the 12:10 base observation does not renew it, runs no `gh pr checks --watch`, exits `stuck - CI pending past 15 minutes`, and the menu replaces the Before `wait [recommended]` row with a numeric `deliver` row scoped to one more 15-minute window with no round charged and neither cap extended, plus `assess` and `stop` last - so ordinary wait is absent and the one-window semantics are explicit. Before failed only because it rendered an ordinary `wait` row 1 (and treated `course`/`rounds_cap`/`syncs_*` as non-schema fields), despite narrating no watch and no renewal. To keep this stable, retain the explicit `deliver - ... one more 15-minute window, no round charged, neither cap extended (rounds N of cap, syncs N of cap)` phrasing and the `stuck - ...` verdict in the shared obstacle template, and keep the 'own push / base observation' renewal distinction in the narration; the only thing to avoid regressing is reintroducing any row labelled `wait` or any renewal language tied to resume/re-entry rather than own push or numeric deliver.

After moves f5 to holds: it names the exit as an obstacle ('stuck - CI pending past 15 minutes'), explicitly declines the watch and any renewal from the base observation or retained course, offers 'deliver - resume the retained course with one additional 15-minute watch window' as a numeric row, states 'A timeout continuation extends neither cap' alongside unchanged 0 of 6 / 0 of 6 usage, and has no wait row with stop recommended last. Keep that wording as-is; the only tightening worth considering is to say 'exactly one additional window' in the deliver row itself so the single-window limit is unambiguous even without the cap sentence.
